subject: Unexpected redistribution of usage across subaccounts — invoice review
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir.g@orchidai.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: accounts-payable@orchidai.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:12:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected redistribution of usage across subaccounts — invoice review

Hi Monica,

Hope you’re well. We received the November invoice this morning (INV-ORC-202611) and noticed ~14% of our ingest/embedding usage was attributed to a subaccount we retired in mid-November (subacct-data-ingest-03). Our internal export shows the calls went to subacct-data-ingest-01 during the period.

This resulted in an unexpected line-item and pushed us over our committed tier. Practical ask: can Redwood share the raw usage attribution for 2026-11-10 -> 2026-11-23 and a short explanation for the redistribution? If this is an internal re-mapping that happened during a config change, we’d like to understand and, if appropriate, request an adjustment.

I’ve attached our export (orchid_usage_export_nov2026.csv) with the calls flagged.

Thanks — appreciate a quick confirmation and estimated SLA for a resolution since we’re on a procurement freeze until this invoice is reconciled.

—Samir
Samir Gupta
Head of Platform Ops, OrchidAI
samir.g@orchidai.com
+1 415 555 0123

[Attachment: orchid_usage_export_nov2026.csv (CSV, 1.8MB)]

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.g@orchidai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected redistribution of usage across subaccounts — invoice review

Hi Samir — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the CSV. I’ve looped in Ben (billing ops) and Vivek (platform) to pull the attribution logs and confirm whether any mid-month reassignment occurred.

What we’ll provide in the next 48 hours:
- Per-request attribution export for 2026-11-10 -> 2026-11-23 (JSON/CSV)
- Ingest routing logs for the date window and a short root-cause summary
- If we identify a metering or attribution error, a proposed credit memo and corrected invoice draft

Ben / Vivek — can you triage? Ben, please prioritize the per-request export; if you need raw telemetry let me know and I’ll get infra to pull the KV logs.

Samir — quick question: did Orchid rotate any API keys or consolidate subaccounts in the second week of November? That helps narrow the mapping.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
+1 650 555 0981

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Samir Gupta <samir.g@orchidai.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected redistribution of usage across subaccounts — invoice review

Hi all,

Quick update from billing/telemetry: we pulled the attribution index and routing logs for the window Samir specified. Preliminary observations:

- There was a routing config change deployed 2026-11-09 03:12 UTC that updated a mapping table used by the ingestion proxy. The deploy itself succeeded, but the mapping rollback path had a mismatched key prefix that caused ~13.7% of requests with legacy API key prefixes to be assigned to a fallback subaccount id (subacct-data-ingest-03).
- The raw request logs show consistent request IDs and timestamps that match Orchid’s attached CSV; we’ll provide the per-request export with the matched request_id to help you reconcile.

Attached for reference: a sanitized extract of the ingest logs and a short repro trace.

Next steps:
1) I’ll attach the complete per-request export for the window (redwood_ingest_logs_202611.iso-stub.txt) and a mapping delta.
2) If you confirm Orchid’s exported rows match our request ids, we’ll prepare a credit memo for the misattributed usage and issue a corrected invoice.

Apologies for the disruption — this looks like a rollback path bug introduced during a small mapping refactor. We’ll also add a watch to prevent future fallback-to-obsolete-subacct assignments.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Billing Operations Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
[Attachment: redwood_ingest_logs_202611.iso-stub.txt (text, 800KB)]

From: Samir Gupta <samir.g@orchidai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: accounts-payable@orchidai.com
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 08:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected redistribution of usage across subaccounts — invoice review

Ben/Monica — thanks for the swift triage. I ran a quick join between our export and the log extract you provided; request_id matches for the sample rows and the timestamps align. Two quick asks before Orchid signs off on a credit:

1) Please confirm the exact tokenization rule that triggered fallback assignment and whether any other customers were affected by the same mapping change. We’ll need this for our audit trail.
2) Can Redwood propose a specific credit amount for the misattributed usage? Orchid is fine with a pro-rated correction for the affected November window — we just need a draft credit memo to unblock AP.

Once we have that, I’ll loop AP and they can approve the adjustment and release the payment for the remaining balance.

—Samir
[Attachment: excerpt_orchid_join_sample.csv (CSV, 12KB)]

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.g@orchidai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, accounts-payable@orchidai.com
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected redistribution of usage across subaccounts — invoice review

Samir — thanks for validating the sample join. Final update and resolution:

Root cause: A mapping rollback path used incorrect key-prefix matching (legacy key prefixes were not normalized before the fallback was applied). This caused ~13.7% of legacy-keyed requests between 2026-11-09 03:12 UTC and 2026-11-10 22:00 UTC to be attributed to subacct-data-ingest-03. The deploy was isolated and has been reverted; we pushed a guard to normalize prefixes in the rollback code path.

Impact and remediation:
- Affected usage: 87,420 tokens (ingest + embedding), which translated to 0.17% of Orchid’s total November token spend but pushed a single line-item over your committed tier threshold.
- Proposed adjustment: full re-attribution of the 87,420 tokens to Orchid’s active subaccount plus a credit memo for the overage line item: USD 1,420.00.
- We’ve generated a corrected invoice (INV-ORC-202611-CORR) and a credit memo (credit-memo-RDW-8342.pdf) attached. If you confirm, Redwood will apply the credit immediately and reissue the invoice; payment terms and due date remain unchanged for the remaining balance.

We’ve also added an automated audit alert for mapping-table deploys to catch similar regressions in the future.

Please reply with a quick ACK and we’ll route the credit memo to your AP.

Thanks again for flagging this — sorry for the noise.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
[Attachment: credit-memo-RDW-8342.pdf (PDF, 34KB)]
